title: Politics & Economics
blurb: Power, the state, wealth, and how we govern ourselves.

planned.title: The Art of War
planned.author: Sun Tzu
planned.note: Thirteen chapters: the supreme excellence is to win without fighting, and every battle is decided before it is joined.

planned.title: Leviathan
planned.author: Thomas Hobbes
planned.note: Hobbes on the state of nature and the social contract — life without authority, 'nasty, brutish, and short.'

planned.title: Two Treatises of Government
planned.author: John Locke
planned.note: Locke on natural rights and government by consent — the philosophy behind modern liberty.

planned.title: The Spirit of the Laws
planned.author: Montesquieu
planned.note: Montesquieu on what makes laws just — and the separation of powers that shaped every later republic.

planned.title: The Social Contract
planned.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
planned.note: Rousseau on freedom and the general will — 'man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.'

planned.title: The Wealth of Nations
planned.author: Adam Smith
planned.note: The founding work of modern economics — the division of labor and the invisible hand.

planned.title: The Federalist Papers
planned.author: Hamilton, Madison & Jay
planned.note: The argument for the American Constitution — the finest writing on how a free republic actually works.

planned.title: On Liberty
planned.author: John Stuart Mill
planned.note: Mill's classic argument for individual freedom against the tyranny of the majority.

planned.title: Capital
planned.author: Karl Marx
planned.note: Marx's anatomy of capitalism — labor, value, and the engine he believed would undo it.

planned.title: The Code of Hammurabi
planned.author: Babylon
planned.note: The oldest great code of law — an eye for an eye, carved in stone four thousand years ago.

planned.title: The Arthashastra
planned.author: Kautilya
planned.note: Kautilya's unsparing manual of statecraft and power — India's answer to Machiavelli, written far earlier.

planned.title: The Han Feizi
planned.author: Han Fei
planned.note: The masterwork of Legalism — order through law and power, the philosophy that unified China.

planned.title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
planned.author: Mary Wollstonecraft
planned.note: The founding work of feminist thought — reason and education are not the property of men.

planned.title: Reflections on the Revolution in France
planned.author: Edmund Burke
planned.note: The founding text of modern conservatism — order, tradition, and the danger of abstraction.

planned.title: A Discourse on Inequality
planned.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
planned.note: Rousseau on how society made men unequal — a seed of the French Revolution.

planned.title: Utopia
planned.author: Sir Thomas More
planned.note: More's book that named the genre — an island of perfect order, half-ideal, half-warning.
